text:
maria: customer reported SSE stream cut with a 429 mid-stream, then client reconnected and was charged for resumed + partial duplicate tokens. customer claim: "we got billed twice for the same output"

jordan: any logs / request ids?

maria: linked X-Request-ID headers: req=rc_17f3, session header X-Session-Id=sess-ptk-44. they hit rate limit at ~2k tokens into stream. snippet from client: `Accept: text/event-stream\nAuthorization: Bearer sk-cust-xxx\nX-Session-Id: sess-ptk-44`

li: quick note — billing attribution is per-token ledger entries created when tokens are persistently committed. if disconnect/resume flow isn't atomic we could double-claim.

maria: reproduced locally with low quota and short TTL on resume claim. repro steps I used:
```
1) open SSE with token A, stream ~2k tokens
2) force midstream 429 from rate-limiter (simulate)
3) client reconnects and does resume with same session id
4) server issues new token-claim for resumed portion but original partial claim never GC'd
```

alex: thanks. can you paste the server log around the 429 and resume?

maria: log (redacted):
```
[2026-02-12T14:03:11Z] req=rc_17f3 sess=sess-ptk-44 tokens_claimed=1987 state=streaming
[2026-02-12T14:03:15Z] req=rc_17f3 rate_limit=exceeded code=429 sent
[2026-02-12T14:03:16Z] req=rc_17f3 sess=sess-ptk-44 connection=closed reason=client-retry
[2026-02-12T14:03:17Z] req=rc_17f3-new sess=sess-ptk-44 resume=attempted tokens_claimed=0
[2026-02-12T14:03:18Z] req=rc_17f3-new sess=sess-ptk-44 tokens_claimed=512 state=streaming
```

jordan: looks like the resume path does a fresh claim without reconciling the previous partial claim. TTL/GC for the original claim didn't fire because it was considered active until explicit release.

li: billing side sees two committed claim records (1987 + 512) for same session window -> duplicate charge.

maria: customer wants an audit and refund. they provided client logs and curl of reconnect: `curl -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-cust-xxx" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?resume=sess-ptk-44"`

ops-bot: alerted #eng-runtime with tag @jordan and created ticket RNW-8345 (high).

jordan: proposed fixes:
- make resume token-claim creation idempotent: if an active claim exists for same session/window, attach the resumed stream to it instead of creating a new claim
- on 429 mid-stream, mark previous claim as "orphaned-pending" and set an immediate short reconciliation window (100ms) before allowing new claims
- add atomic ledger write: claim + stream attach in same DB transaction

alex: for short-term mitigation we can:
- bump the claim GC to 1s for streams under heavy retry patterns
- add a countermeasure: if reconnect comes within 500ms with same X-Session-Id, treat it as continuation (no new billing claim)

maria: customer asked for repro to validate fix. jordan, can you add a deterministic test in runtime that simulates midstream 429 + immediate reconnect?

jordan: yes — I'll add an integration test that asserts single ledger entry for session on resume. will also include a stress case for burst reconnects. planning patch, will post PR link when ready.

li: once PR is up, I'll run billing replay to reconcile affected accounts and prepare refunds if ledger shows double commits.

maria: thanks all — keeping customer updated. cc @alex for support follow-up notes. :thumbsup:
